reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — the hard gate has no working measurement
gaps.problem: §5's group A/B is the sanctioned and exclusive way to measure transit's draw calls and triangles (item 1's hard gate, item 16's culling check, and the stats().draws cross-check all route through it), and the snippet does not work. It reads __sim.stats().drawCalls, sets g.visible=false, and reads again — synchronously, with no frame rendered in between. The comments say 'render one frame' but __sim exposes no render()/step(); engine writes stats at the end of each rAF render (engine.js:64) with info.autoReset=true. Pasted into page.evaluate as written it returns transitDraws = 0 every time, i.e. transit passes its primary budget gate unconditionally. A critic who patches it will guess at one rAF or two and get different answers.
gaps.fix: Make the snippet async and await real frames: `const frame = () => new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r)));` then `await frame(); const on = __sim.stats().drawCalls; g.visible=false; await frame(); const off = __sim.stats().drawCalls; g.visible=true; await frame();` — two rAFs per read because stats are written at the end of the render that follows the visibility change. State that the probe must run under headless=1 where the loop keeps rendering at speed=0, and repeat the same shape for .triangles.

gaps.problem: §2 fixes `ridership` as 'passengers per game day' — a daily total. Item 10 then requires `ridership` at 08:00 to be ≥ 2× `ridership` at 02:00, which only makes sense if it is an instantaneous hourly rate, and in the same item asserts `boardings(24) === Σ ridership over all active lines ± 5 %`, which only closes if it is a daily total. It cannot be both. The HUD prints it as 'N / day' and divides by vehicles×60×8 for utilisation (hud.js), so the panel reads it as a daily total too. A builder must guess; whichever they pick, the other half of item 10 fails, and the critic and builder then argue about which reading was meant. `balance = ridership × fare − vehicles × 900` in ¢/month compounds it by multiplying a per-day figure into a monthly one with no stated conversion.
gaps.fix: Split the two quantities. Keep `ridership` on the line record as the daily total (constant across the hour probe) and add a separate `stats().rate(h)` or `line.rateNow` for the hour-of-day rate. Rewrite the 08:00/02:00 assertion against that rate field, keep `boardings(24) === Σ ridership ± 5 %` against the daily total, and say explicitly whether `balance` uses ridership × 30 days or ridership as-is.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — no lower bound anywhere on how fast a bus moves
gaps.problem: Item 8's arc-advance test is `arcLength(pose(12.25)) − arcLength(pose(12.0)) == 900 s × stats().meanSpeed ± 5 %`. `meanSpeed` is reported by the module itself. The spec explicitly rejects self-reported numbers for draw calls ('stats().draws, which is transit reporting its own compliance — unfalsifiable') and then makes the central motion test self-referential: whatever the fleet actually does, the module reports that as meanSpeed and the identity holds. Item 7 only caps speed from above (≤ type.speed/3.6) and requires monotonic t. A fleet crawling at 0.4 m/s satisfies items 7 and 8 completely, produces a 1.2–3.5 km loop that never completes, and yet §8's 'no camera sees fewer than 2 buses' still passes.
gaps.fix: Bound meanSpeed independently: `stats().meanSpeed ∈ [6, 14] m/s` (a 50 km/h street minus 6–12 s dwell at 6–12 stops lands there), and add the derived check that a vehicle completes ≥ 1 full circuit between hour 12.0 and 12.25 for a loop of ≤ 3.5 km. Then the ±5 % identity is a consistency check on a number that is itself pinned.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) / conflict — item 16's chunking rule is either vacuous or contradicts the 20-draw budget
gaps.problem: Item 16 requires 'Instanced content is chunked to TILE_SIZE = 128 m groups' and grades it via 'every instanced chunk has a finite geometry.boundingSphere whose radius ≤ 1.5 × TILE_SIZE (192 m)'. For an InstancedMesh, `geometry.boundingSphere` is the source geometry's — a single bus is ~6 m, a shelter ~2 m — so an entirely unchunked mesh spanning the whole 700 m network passes the probe trivially. The instance-cloud sphere lives on `mesh.boundingSphere`, not `geometry.boundingSphere`. If the rule is read the other way (chunk for real), 18 stops and 4 routes over a 700 m box fall into roughly 30 tiles, and per-tile InstancedMeshes make shelter frame + shelter glass + ribbons alone blow past the ≤ 20 ceiling — directly contradicting §5's indicative split ('shelter frame 1, shelter glass 1, route ribbons 1–2') and item 16's own 'route ribbons for all lines merge into ≤ 2 draw calls'. Two competent builders diverge here: one chunks and fails item 1, one does not and passes item 16.
gaps.fix: Say which surfaces are chunked and which are single-batch, and grade the right property. E.g.: 'ribbons, chips, discs and chevrons are single merged batches (≤ 2 + 1 + 1 draws) and are exempt from chunking; buses and shelters are chunked only if the module exceeds 12 draws unchunked. Probe `mesh.boundingSphere` (call `mesh.computeBoundingSphere()`, not the geometry's) and require radius ≤ 192 m on any chunked InstancedMesh, and ≤ 400 m on the exempt merged batches.' Keep the off-screen-camera test as the real culling gate, since that one works.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — item 4's legal stop band excludes the position props actually puts its shelter at
gaps.problem: Item 4 grades stop seating as `asphaltHalf + 0.5 ≤ nearestEdge().dist ≤ asphaltHalf + sidewalk` — for a `street`, 5.5–8.0 m from the centreline. The standing assumptions correctly state (and place.js:290 confirms) that props places its `bus_stop` at `asphaltHalf + sidewalk + 1.35` = 9.35 m on a street: 1.35 m outside the band item 4 declares legal. So an adopted stop whose furniture is the props shelter must still keep its own record ≥ 1.35 m away from that shelter to pass item 4, which is satisfiable inside the 6 m adoption radius but is never said anywhere. A builder who reasonably co-locates the stop record with the shelter it adopts fails item 4 on every adopted stop — precisely the stops item 13 rewards them for creating.
gaps.fix: Add one sentence to item 4: 'For a stop with `propId !== null`, the stop record still sits inside the band above (on the sidewalk); the adopted props shelter sits ~1.35 m further out in the verge (place.js:290) and is not graded on this band. Expect roughly 1.3–2 m between the stop disc and the adopted shelter and frame the `stop` preset accordingly.'

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — two probes measure the scene rather than the thing
gaps.problem: (a) Item 3's sparkle probe crops a 200×200 px box centred on a bus at `aerial`. At distance 520 with fov 45° over 1080 px that is ~2.5 px/m, so a 12 m bus is roughly 30×8 px inside an 80 m × 80 m crop of city — the isolated-pixel test then fires on lane markings, lamp heads and props foliage and fails or passes for reasons unrelated to transit. (b) Item 5 requires `setOverlay(false)` to change '0 pixels outside the road network' at aerial, but the spec itself disqualifies `isRoad()` as too coarse (4 m grid) and offers no other road mask, while item 19's stop-name chips and the ribbon's 0.15 m outline necessarily change pixels off the asphalt. As written 'exactly 0' is both unmeasurable and unachievable.
gaps.fix: (a) Size the crop to the target: crop the projected screen-space AABB of the bus dilated by 8 px (typically ~46×24 px at aerial), or move the sparkle test to `closeup`/`bus` where the vehicle fills a meaningful fraction of the frame. (b) Replace 'and 0 pixels outside the road network' with a bounded version the critic can actually compute: 'and ≤ 0.4 % of screen pixels change more than 60 m from any edge polyline, measured by distance to `world.roads.sample` samples — the ribbon and its outline are on the carriageway; chips are exempt.'

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — the props triangle figure is wrong, and wrong twice in two different directions
gaps.problem: Standing assumptions state props 'budgets 400 draw calls / 2.2 M triangles (`src/modules/props/index.js:143-144`)'. That exact line reads `budget: { drawCalls: 400, triangles: 1_900_000 }`. §5 of the same spec then says props' 'own spec caps it at 700 k triangles and 400 draws in a showcase shot' — and props.md:447/451 declares `{drawCalls: 400, triangles: 900_000}` with ≤ 700 000 attributable. So the document carries three mutually inconsistent numbers for the one figure its whole frame-total headroom argument (≤ 3 M, item 21) rests on. It is the only citation of the ~20 I checked that does not match its cited line, which makes it more dangerous, not less: a builder who has learned to trust the line references will trust this one.
gaps.fix: Correct the standing assumption to '400 draw calls / 1 900 000 triangles declared (`props/index.js:143-144`); props.md caps attributable triangles at ≤ 700 000 in a showcase shot (props.md:451), which is the figure to plan the frame total against', and make §5's headroom paragraph cite the same number.

gaps.property: 1 (sequenced) — no round-1 floor for a 22-item list built from an 11-line stub
gaps.problem: Round 1 starts from a stub with `api: {serialize, deserialize}`. The spec asks for 22 acceptance items covering ~80 distinct assertions: a modelled bus at cs2_5 quality with 2 LOD levels, a modelled shelter, an adoption path, Dijkstra routing with a 40 ms budget, hour-pure vehicle pose, ridership modelling, save/load with re-derived propIds, chips at 720p, plus a tram. Only item 22 carries a stated weight ('a miss costs at most 0.3, build 1–21 first'). Nothing tells the builder what round 1 must clear versus what may land in round 2 or 3, so the likely outcome is broad shallow coverage — exactly the shape a critic scores a 6 on and a round is spent unwinding.
gaps.fix: Add one paragraph after the acceptance list: 'Round 1 must clear items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14, 20, 21 (the contract, the seating, the overlay, repeatability, the HUD, adoption, save/load, the gates). Items 3, 6, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 are the round-2 quality pass. Item 22 is round 3+. A round-1 submission that spreads thin across all 22 scores worse than one that clears the first list cleanly.'

gaps.property: role-file separation (standard §'Rules for role prompts') — invariants restated where they will drift
gaps.problem: The header promises 'everything invariant … lives there and is not repeated here', then repeats several BUILDER.md invariants verbatim: the no-lights / no-toneMapping / no-composer / no-renderer.render rule (standing assumptions, bullet 5 vs BUILDER.md 'Stay in your lane'), 'all randomness through ctx.rng / ctx.rng.fork(label); no Date.now()/performance.now() outside profiling' (item 20 vs BUILDER.md 'Determinism'), and 'zero per-frame allocation in update() — reuse vectors/matrices/arrays allocated in init()' (§5 vs BUILDER.md 'No per-frame allocation'). Each will drift the day BUILDER.md changes, and the spec's own header is then false. Note this is mild: each restatement adds something transit-specific (headlights must be emissive geometry, a 0.5 MB/600-frame heap probe, a byte-identical serialize test).
gaps.fix: Keep only the transit-specific delta and point at the role file for the rest: 'Lights: BUILDER.md's lane rule applies — transit's headlights, taillights, interior glow, blinds and shelter lamp are emissive geometry and projected decals, never PointLight/SpotLight.' Same for item 20 ('BUILDER.md determinism applies; transit-specific: two loads at ?seed=1337 produce byte-identical api.serialize()…') and the §5 allocation row (keep the numeric probe, drop the restated rule).

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — small measurement wording that will cost minutes rather than rounds
gaps.problem: Item 1 demands `status === 'ready'` in 'all 16 gauntlet shots', but CRITIC.md's prescribed command is `--times 12,22`, which produces 8; the 16-shot matrix is gauntlet.mjs's default, so the critic must know to drop the --times flag. Item 2 phrases the seating check as 'stop y within [roadY + 0.10, roadY + 0.30] of world.roads.sample(...).y', which reads as a tolerance band around a band. Item 3 says to project the bus with 'camera.project()' — in three.js that is `vector.project(camera)`, and `__sim.camera` is the rig, not the THREE camera (`__sim.camera.camera`).
gaps.fix: Item 1: 'all 16 gauntlet shots (`node tools/gauntlet.mjs --module transit --round <n>` with its default 4 cameras × 6.5/12/17.5/22 — do not pass --times)'. Item 2: 'stop.y − world.roads.sample(edgeId, t).y ∈ [0.10, 0.30] m'. Item 3: 'project with `new THREE.Vector3(x,y,z).project(__sim.camera.camera)`'.

strengths: Code archaeology is real, not decorative. I spot-checked every line citation I could: hud.js:25 (LINE_COLOURS), hud.js:892 (_lines prefers transitSource), hud.js 905/912/929/934/942-944 (the exact ui:action verbs), hud.js:316 (transitLines), hud.js:458 (the broken tools?.api?.select), network.js:6-11 (TYPE_DEFAULTS reproduced field-for-field including asphaltHalf/sidewalk), network.js:88-91 (_bump emits roads:changed on every addNode/addEdge), network.js:285-296 (install() puts exactly 8 functions on the section), place.js:283-297 (bus_stop at street|avenue, len>66, p=0.38, t=0.42, offset asphaltHalf+sidewalk+1.35), props/index.js:44-55/190/199/234-249, registry.js:15, camera.js:74-76 (_clamp per-axis to 1224), main.js:82, screenshot.mjs:22, engine.js:64, build.js:121/513-559, props.md:103/652, tools.md:93-95, ui.md:39. All correct except one (see gaps). This is the difference between a spec that describes the codebase and one that has actually read it.

It correctly refuses to paraphrase what ARCHITECTURE cannot supply. §3 has no transit section at all and §15 says only 'Owns world.transit'; rather than inventing a contract and calling it copied, §2 says so and anchors the field names to what shipped ui/hud.js already reads, with the reason (renaming any of them silently blanks the panel). Where ARCHITECTURE §3 and the implementation disagree (isRoad advertised 0..1, implemented 0/1/2 on a 4 m grid) it names the divergence and rules the function out as a grading instrument.

The visual anchors are checkable and verified. I opened $REF/cs2_1.jpg and cs2_5.jpg: the overlay description (white dashed polyline, translucent saturated blue fill, small dark rounded chips reading '39 m', '-7.7 %', '¢616') and the vehicle description (near-black glasshouse separate from body, red rear lamp cluster, pale plate, clearcoat streak) are literal transcriptions of those frames, not remembered impressions. Property 4 is genuinely satisfied.

Known failure modes (§6) are project history, not generic advice. Every one of the first eight traces to a real finding in docs/critic/ (environment_r1 tiling lattice and washed noon, roads_r1 washed noon / floating-sunk / grass through asphalt, effects_r1 'night is a milky blue dusk', terrain_r1 std 8.8 milky aerial, simulation_r1 lawn tiling and 720p clipping, ui_r1 720p overflow) and each is restated as the symptom it would take on a bus roof or a ribbon.

The camera presets are arithmetically valid against the real rig. All six §8 presets use the {position, target} form that camera.apply() actually supports (camera.js:38-44), and every one lands inside minDistance 8 / minPitch 0.08 / maxPitch 1.5 when I worked out the implied distance and pitch. Item 16's off-screen camera (1200,200,1200) was clearly checked against _clamp's per-axis 1224 m limit rather than assumed.

It anticipates the round-1 blocker instead of discovering it in round 2. The whole 'props is shipped and will populate this showcase' thread — adoption within 6 m, propId re-derived on deserialize because props.serialize() only stores {version, seed}, no writes into world.props — is the single most valuable thing in the document and is graded today (item 13), not deferred to a shim.
verdict: 8.0 — FAIL by the ≥ 8.5 bar, but a near miss that a short edit pass closes. This is the most thoroughly researched module spec I have reviewed in this repo: I verified roughly twenty of its source citations against the actual files and only one (props' triangle budget) was wrong, and I opened two of the CS2 reference frames and found the visual anchors transcribed literally rather than remembered. Properties 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are satisfied, §6 is grounded in real findings from six critic reports rather than generic advice, and the props-adoption thread anticipates what would otherwise certainly have been the round-1 blocker. What holds it under the bar is not vagueness — it is five places where the machinery is stated so confidently that nobody will notice it does not close. The §5 group A/B is the only sanctioned measurement of the module's primary budget and, as written, returns 0 every time because no frame is rendered between the two reads; item 10 defines `ridership` as a daily total in §2 and then grades it as an hourly rate; item 8's central motion test is anchored to a number the module reports about itself, leaving no lower bound on how fast a bus moves; item 16's chunking rule is vacuous as probed and contradicts the 20-draw ceiling if probed correctly; and item 4's legal seating band excludes, by 1.35 m, the exact position props puts the shelter transit is being rewarded for adopting. Those are builder guesses and critic arguments, not judgement calls — each is worth a round. Fix those five plus the props triangle figure and add a round-1 floor, and this is a 9.
